en.Las agencias espaciales del mundo buscan: The world's space agencies are looking for a new mission director.
en.Alguien capaz de equilibrar presupuesto,: Someone who can balance budget, mass, power and science...
en....y de tomar decisiones que podrían cam: ...and make decisions that could change history.
en.Tu astronauta, Albertsahur, te espera en: Your astronaut, Albertsahur, is waiting for you in the design room.
en.¡Hola, director! Soy Albertsahur, tu ast: Hello, director! I'm Albertsahur, your astronaut. Before we lift off, we have to pick our spacecraft.
en.A la izquierda están las stats: propulsi: On the left are the stats: propulsion, power, mass capacity, science and communications.
Up on the right is the budget. Every ship costs a different amount, and whatever is left we'll spend on instruments and equipment.
en.Usa las flechas < > para comparar las na: Use the < > arrows to compare the ships. Careful: the priciest one isn't always the best choice.
Once you've made up your mind, press CHOOSE SHIP. I'll be waiting!
en.¡Excelente elección! La %s ya está en la: Excellent choice! The %s is already out on the launch pad.
en.Nos quedan %s para el resto de la misión: We have %s left for the rest of the mission. Let's head to the workshop and outfit her!
en.(La pantalla del taller todavía no exist: (The workshop screen doesn't exist yet. That's the next thing to build!)
en.Nave pequeña y barata para misiones cort: A small, cheap spacecraft for short missions in orbit.
Gemini IV is tiny but reliable. It's the ship that made the first American spacewalk. Cheap, but it won't take us far and it can't carry much.
en.El cohete más poderoso de su época. Pued: The most powerful rocket of its day. It can reach the Moon.
en.¡El Saturn V! Con él llegamos a la Luna: The Saturn V! This is the rocket that first took us to the Moon. Huge thrust and payload, but it eats up a big chunk of the budget.
en.Tecnología moderna: paneles solares y co: Modern technology: solar panels and top-notch communications.
en.Artemis II lleva cuatro tripulantes alre: Artemis II carries four crew members around the Moon. It's the most modern ship and the best for power and communications... but it leaves you almost no money for anything else.
en.PROPULSIÓN: motores más potentes. La nav: PROPULSION: stronger engines. The ship climbs faster and reaches the exosphere sooner.
en.ENERGÍA: alimenta un escudo protector. C: POWER: feeds a protective shield. Every 40 points of power absorbs one hit without costing you hull.
en.CAP. DE MASA: casco más fuerte, aguanta: MASS CAP.: a tougher hull that takes more hits... but the ship gets heavier and moves sideways more slowly.
en.CIENCIA: más instrumentos. Juntamos más: SCIENCE: more instruments. We gather more data in every layer of the atmosphere, and that means more points at the end.
en.COMUNICACIONES: el centro de control nos: COMMUNICATIONS: mission control warns us before lightning strikes. At 50 or more, it also warns us where planes and satellites are coming from.
en.¡Bienvenido al taller, director! Aquí eq: Welcome to the workshop, director! This is where we outfit the %s before launch.
en.Toca un stat a la izquierda y compra una: Tap a stat on the left and buy an upgrade on the right: minimal, medium or maximum. No stat can go above 100.
en.Cada stat cambia el vuelo: propulsión su: Every stat changes the flight: propulsion climbs faster, power gives shields, mass gives hull strength, communications gives warnings and science gives points.
en.Ojo: el dinero que no gastes también sum: Careful: the money you don't spend also counts for points at the end. Choose wisely!
en.¡Listo! Mejora %s instalada: %s sube de: Done! %s upgrade installed: %s goes from %d up to %d.
en.(Solo se aprovecharon %d puntos porque: (Only %d points were used, because 100 is the cap.)
en.Desinstalamos la última mejora y te devo: We removed the last upgrade and you got %s back.
en.Ahora llegaremos a la exosfera en unos %: Now we'll reach the exosphere in about %d seconds of full-throttle flight.
en.El escudo protector aguantará %d golpe(s: The protective shield will take %d hit(s) before the hull starts taking damage.
en.El casco aguanta %d golpes, y la maniobr: The hull takes %d hits, and handling came out %s.
en.Juntaremos %d puntos de datos en cada ca: We'll gather %d data points in every layer of the atmosphere.
en.¡Y ya nos avisarán de dónde vienen avio: And now they'll warn us where planes and satellites are coming from!
en.Tendremos %.1f segundos de aviso antes d: We'll get %.1f seconds of warning before every lightning bolt.%s
en.¡La %s está lista! Vamos a la plataforma: The %s is ready! Let's head out to the launch pad.
(I can't find the launch scene. Check that ascenso.tscn is in res://scenes/)
en.Plataforma lista, director. Estamos en e: Pad is ready, director. We're at the Kennedy Space Center, in Florida.
en.La nave sube sola: tú usa las flechas IZ: The ship climbs on its own: you use the LEFT and RIGHT arrows to dodge. Starting the countdown!
en.Esta es la troposfera: empieza en el sue: This is the troposphere: it starts at the ground, and almost all our weather happens here.
en.Entre más subimos, más frío: de unos 17: The higher we climb, the colder it gets: from about 17 °C down here to -51 °C up top. Watch out for planes and lightning!
en.¡Pasamos la tropopausa! Esta es la estra: We've crossed the tropopause! This is the stratosphere, and it reaches up to about 50 km.
en.Aquí se forma el ozono, y eso calienta e: Ozone forms here, and that warms the air: the temperature RISES with altitude. Dodge the balloons!
en.Mesosfera: de 50 a 85 km. Aquí vuelve a: Mesosphere: 50 to 85 km. Up here it gets colder again the higher we go.
en.El aire todavía frena a los meteoros: se: The air still slows meteors down: they burn up and leave trails of fire. Watch out for the meteors!
en.Termosfera: de 85 a 600 km. Absorbe rayo: Thermosphere: 85 to 600 km. It soaks up X-rays and ultraviolet light from the Sun and reaches up to 2,000 °C.
en.Pero el aire es tan delgado que no senti: But the air is so thin we wouldn't even feel that heat. Grab the shields to repair the ship!
en.¡Exosfera! Va de unos 600 hasta 10,000 k: The exosphere! It runs from about 600 up to 10,000 km. Up here atoms escape into space.
This is the layer where satellites orbit. Don't crash into them!
en.¡Lo logramos, director! Atravesamos toda: We made it, director! We've crossed the whole atmosphere. We're in space!
en.La nave no aguantó... Revisemos el diseñ: The ship couldn't take it... Let's go over the design and try again.
en.¡Cuidado! Nos queda un solo punto de res: Careful! We're down to a single point of hull strength.
en.¡Escudo recuperado! Eso repara un punto: Shield recovered! That repairs one point of hull strength.

en.¡Director, alerta del control de misión!: Director, alert from mission control! The Sun just fired off an X-class solar flare, one of the strongest kinds there is.
en.Detrás viene una eyección de masa corona: Right behind it comes a coronal mass ejection: a giant cloud of charged particles heading straight for us.
en.Esa radiación daña la electrónica y a la: That radiation damages electronics and the crew. Everyone to the shelter, the most heavily shielded part of the ship! Sealing the hatches...
en.Apagamos todo lo que no es indispensable: We shut down everything that isn't essential and sit in the dark, pressed up against the shielding.
en.Shhh... Ahora solo queda esperar a que p: Shhh... Now all we can do is wait for the radiation to pass.
en....Uf. Los sensores de radiación ya baja: ...Phew. The radiation sensors are dropping. The storm has passed.
en.Salimos del refugio, revisamos los siste: We come out of the shelter, check the systems, and everything is still in order. We're almost at the Moon!
en.Lo anoté en la bitácora, director. Ábrel: I wrote it down in the logbook, director. Open it from the pause menu to learn more about solar flares.
en.Ya vamos rumbo a la Luna, director. Son: We're on our way to the Moon, director. It's about a 3-day trip, almost all of it with the engines off.
en.Desde la cabina vigilamos el oxígeno, el: From the cabin we keep an eye on oxygen, fuel and the hull. If something fails, we have to fix it fast.
en.Ojo: la Gemini IV es pequeña y vieja. Su: Careful: Gemini IV is small and old. Its valves fail often and the thrusters respond with a bit of a lag.
en.Ojo: la computadora del Apollo tiene muy: Careful: the Apollo computer has very little memory. If it gets too much data it overloads... like the famous 1202 alarm.
en.Artemis es muy confiable, pero la radiac: Artemis is very reliable, but deep-space radiation scrambles its computer. And if something does fail, it all fails at once.
en.Día 2. La Tierra ya se ve chiquita por l: Day 2. Earth already looks tiny through the window. We keep drifting quietly toward the Moon.
en.Día 3. ¡La Luna se ve cada vez más grand: Day 3. The Moon looks bigger and bigger! We're almost there.
en.¡Falla en las válvulas de oxígeno! En el: Oxygen valve failure! On Apollo 13 an oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon.
en.Elige una válvula (1, 2 o 3) y gira el r: Pick a valve (1, 2 or 3) and turn the regulator with A/D or by dragging the mouse until the needle sits in the green.
en.¡Basura espacial en la ruta! Un pedacito: Space debris on our path! A chunk the size of a nut can punch straight through the hull.
en.La NASA hace maniobras de evasión con im: NASA makes evasion maneuvers with short bursts. Move with the arrow keys, but every move burns fuel.
en.¡Tormenta solar! El Sol lanzó una eyecci: Solar storm! The Sun has fired off a coronal mass ejection: radiation that damages electronics and the crew.
en.Baja la palanca del escudo de plomo y ma: Pull down the lead shield lever and hold DEPLOY to close the windows.
en.¡Alarma 1202! En el Apollo 11 la computa: 1202 alarm! On Apollo 11 the computer overloaded during the descent to the Moon.
en.Por suerte sabía descartar lo menos impo: Luckily it knew how to drop the least important tasks. Kill the junk processes (amber), but don't touch the vital ones (green)!
en.¡Falla crítica de oxígeno! La válvula pr: Critical oxygen failure! The main valve is jammed. On Apollo 13 an oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon.
en.Abre las 3 válvulas auxiliares: mantén p: Open the 3 backup valves: hold each one down until its ring fills up green. Every second you take, we lose oxygen!
en.¡Falla en la distribución eléctrica! Si: Power distribution failure! If the power goes down, life support shuts off.
en.Enciende todos los switches de la matriz: Flip every switch in the grid back on. While any are off the batteries drain... and some of them will trip again on their own!
en.Perdimos la señal con la Tierra. Mientra: We've lost the signal with Earth. The farther we get, the weaker it arrives.
en.La NASA usa la Red del Espacio Profundo: NASA uses the Deep Space Network to talk to its spacecraft. Line the green wave up with the blue one using W/S and A/D.
en.¡Válvulas estables! El oxígeno vuelve a: Valves are stable! Oxygen is climbing again.
en.¡Esquivamos todo! Ni un rasguño en el ca: We dodged everything! Not a scratch on the hull.
en.¡Escudo cerrado! Nos refugiamos hasta qu: Shield closed! We take cover until the storm blows over.
en.¡CPU bajo control! La computadora vuelve: CPU under control! The computer is guiding us again.
en.¡Válvulas abiertas! El oxígeno vuelve a: Valves are open! Oxygen is flowing back into the cabin.
en.¡Energía restaurada! Todos los sistemas: Power restored! Every system is back online.
en.¡Enlace restablecido! Ya estamos mandand: Link re-established! We're sending data back to Earth again.
en.Nos pegaron algunas rocas. El casco qued: A few rocks got us. The hull is down to %d%%.
en.¡La radiación nos alcanzó! Se alteraron: The radiation caught us! The monitors scrambled and we lost science data.
en.La computadora nos desvió de la ruta. Ga: The computer pushed us off course. We burned fuel correcting it and lost time.
en.No abrimos todas las válvulas a tiempo y: We didn't open every valve in time and lost a lot of oxygen. We have to be careful!
We didn't restore all the power in time. The batteries are down to %d%%.
en.No logramos alinear bien la antena. La s: We couldn't line the antenna up properly. The signal is weak: we'll gather less data.
The hull couldn't take the impacts.
en.Nos quedamos sin energía y se apagaron t: We ran out of power and every system shut down.
That didn't go well, but we're still going.
en.¡Ya vemos la Luna enorme por la ventana!: The Moon fills the whole window now! Get ready for the arrival maneuver.
en.Revisemos el diseño de la nave e intent: Let's go over the ship's design and try again.

en.¡Salimos de la atmósfera! Ahora estamos: We're out of the atmosphere! Now we're in orbit around the Earth.
en.Vamos a casi 28,000 km/h. Estamos cayend: We're doing almost 28,000 km/h. We're falling toward Earth the whole time, but we're moving sideways so fast that we never hit it: that's what an orbit is.
en.No salimos directo al espacio. Primero d: We don't head straight out into space. First we loop around in a 'parking orbit' to check that every system is working properly.
en.También esperamos el momento justo: cuan: We also wait for exactly the right moment: when our destination lines up, we use the speed we already have and burn less fuel.
en.Así lo hizo el Apollo 11 en 1969: dio un: That's what Apollo 11 did in 1969: it circled the Earth one and a half times before lighting the engine toward the Moon.
en.Artemis II también revisa sus sistemas d: Artemis II also checks its systems while circling the Earth before firing its engines toward the Moon.
en.Dato curioso: la Gemini IV real nunca sa: Fun fact: the real Gemini IV never left orbit; it spent 4 days circling the Earth. We're going farther than that!
en.¡Ahora! Encendemos motores hasta unos 40: Now! We fire the engines up to about 40,000 km/h: Earth's escape velocity.
en.A esa velocidad la gravedad ya no puede: At that speed gravity can't pull us back anymore. Goodbye, Earth! Next stop, the Moon!
en.¡Mira cómo se hace chiquita la Tierra! L: Look how small the Earth is getting! The Moon is about 384,400 km away.
en.Casi todo el camino vamos con los motore: We coast almost the whole way with the engines off: the push we got carries us there.
en.Llegamos. Si no hacemos nada, pasaríamos: We've arrived. If we do nothing, we'd sail right past. We turn the ship around and fire the engine backwards to brake.
en.Así la gravedad de la Luna nos atrapa: ¡: That way the Moon's gravity catches us: we're in lunar orbit!
en.La gravedad de la Luna es como una sexta: The Moon's gravity is about one sixth of Earth's. That's why astronauts look like they're bouncing when they walk.
en.Ahora el módulo lunar 'Eagle' se separa: Now the lunar module 'Eagle' separates with two astronauts, while the third one stays up in orbit.
en.'El Águila ha aterrizado.' El 20 de juli: 'The Eagle has landed.' On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11 touched down in the Sea of Tranquility.
en.¡Misión cumplida, director! Llegamos a l: Mission accomplished, director! We made it to the Moon.
en.¡Ahora te toca a ti, director! Toma los: Now it's your turn, director! Take the controls and set her down gently.
en.Dato curioso: ninguna Gemini fue a la Lu: Fun fact: no Gemini ever went to the Moon. They were used to practice in orbit the maneuvers the Apollo program would later need.
en.¡Pero en nuestra misión sí lo logramos!: But on our mission we pulled it off! Mission accomplished, director!
en.Artemis II no frena para quedarse: usa u: Artemis II doesn't brake to stay: it uses a free-return trajectory.
en.Le damos la vuelta a la Luna por su lado: We swing around the far side of the Moon and its gravity sends us back toward Earth all by itself, with almost no fuel.
en.¡Vimos el lado oculto de la Luna! Ahora: We've seen the far side of the Moon! Now we head home. Mission accomplished, director!
en.¡Después de 3 días de viaje, ya estamos: After 3 days of travel, we're finally reaching the Moon!
